docs.title: Rivet Language Docs
docs.text:
Welcome to the user documentation for Rivet v0.0.1.

If you want to write programs in Rivet today, this site shows what works, how to run it, and where current limits are.

docs.title: Start Here
docs.text:
1. Go to Getting Started for build + first run.
  2. Read Language Basics for syntax you will use most.
  3. Use Reference when you need a quick rule or keyword lookup.

docs.title: What You Can Build Today
docs.text:
• Integer and string variables
  • Fixed-size integer arrays
  • References and optional references (ref, optref, address_of, deref, null)
  • Expressions with arithmetic, comparisons, and keyword operators (and, or, lsft, rsft)
  • Control flow with if/else, while, and for
  • Functions with fun and return
  • Multi-file programs with import module;

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int sum = 0;

  for (i in 0 to 4 step 1) {
    sum = sum + i;
  }

  return sum;
}

docs.title: Current Limits You Should Know
docs.text:
• Error messages are improving, but some are still terse.
  • Imports are path-convention based (lib/ and ../lib/ fallback).
  • Some edge cases in arrays/refs/strings are still under active validation.

docs.title: Version
docs.text: This documentation targets Rivet v0.0.1.

docs.title: Cortex-M0 Simulation
docs.text: This page describes the current demo assets for embedded-style experimentation.

docs.title: What Is Included
docs.text:
Under examples/basic_test/ and examples/uart_test/, the repo includes:

  • linker scripts
  • startup assembly
  • generated objects/ELF artifacts
  • Renode run scripts (run.resc)

docs.title: Typical Flow
docs.text:
1. Compile your Rivet program with ./build/rivet <file>.rvt.
  2. Use your target toolchain/linker flow with the provided linker/startup assets.
  3. Run simulation through the Renode script in the example folder.

docs.title: Note
docs.text: The exact simulation command may depend on your local Renode setup. Use the included run.resc files as the baseline entry point.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Short examples you can run as starting points.

docs.title: 1. Function + Return
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int a = 10;
  int b = 20;
  return a + b;
}

docs.title: 2. If / Else
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int value = 7;

  if (value == 7) {
    value = value + 1;
  } else {
    value = value - 1;
  }

  return value;
}

docs.title: 3. While Loop
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int i = 0;
  int sum = 0;

  while (i < 5) {
    sum = sum + i;
    i = i + 1;
  }

  return sum;
}

docs.title: 4. For Range Loop
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int sum = 0;

  for (i in 0 to 5 step 1) {
    sum = sum + i;
  }

  return sum;
}

docs.title: 5. Arrays
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int[4] nums;
  nums[0] = 1;
  nums[1] = 2;
  nums[2] = 3;
  nums[3] = 4;

  return nums[0] + nums[1] + nums[2] + nums[3];
}

docs.title: 6. References and Optional References
docs.text:
fun int main() {
  int base = 42;
  int ref ptr = address_of base;
  int optref maybe = null;

  return deref ptr;
}

docs.title: 7. Import + Intrinsic
docs.text:
import dummy;

fun int main() {
  __volatile_store(0x40021000, 1);
  return imported_x;
}

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide is for developers who want to write and run Rivet programs right now.

docs.title: Quick Install (Prebuilt Binary)
docs.text:
Latest release:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diveshkshirsagar/RIVET/main/install.sh | bash

Specific version:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diveshkshirsagar/RIVET/main/install.sh | RIVET_VERSION=v0.0.1 bash

Default install target is /usr/local/bin, so rivet is available as a normal shell command.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• CMake >= 3.16
  • A C++17 compiler
  • LLVM installed with CMake package config available

docs.title: Build the Compiler
docs.text:
From repository root:

cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -j

This creates the compiler binary at build/rivet.

docs.title: Your First Program
docs.text:
Create a file like hello.rvt:

fun int main() {
  int a = 2;
  int b = 3;
  return a + b;
}

Run it:

./build/rivet hello.rvt

docs.title: Useful Run Modes
docs.text:
Print AST while compiling:

./build/rivet hello.rvt --dump-ast

Compile using explicit target settings:

./build/rivet hello.rvt \
  --target=arm-none-eabi \
  --mcpu=cortex-m0

Optional memory layout flags:

./build/rivet hello.rvt \
  --flash-origin=0x08000000 \
  --flash-size=512K \
  --ram-origin=0x20000000 \
  --ram-size=128K

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
1. Write .rvt file.
  2. Run ./build/rivet <file>.rvt.
  3. If needed, rerun with --dump-ast for debugging syntax/structure.
  4. Iterate using examples in tests/ and examples/.

docs.title: Where to Go Next
docs.text:
• Language Basics for variables, control flow, and functions.
  • Features for memory, modules, and types.
  • Reference for syntax/keywords lookup.

docs.title: Standard Library
docs.text: Rivet v0.0.1 does not ship with a stable standard library yet.

docs.title: What Exists Today
docs.text:
• Module-style source reuse through import <module>;
  • Project-local library files typically placed in lib/
  • Compiler intrinsic call support for low-level operations such as:
  • __volatile_store(address, value)

docs.title: Recommended Practice
docs.text:
• Keep reusable helpers in small lib/*.rvt modules.
  • Import only what you need per program.
  • Treat module APIs as evolving while the language stabilizes.

This page will be expanded once standard library modules are formalized.

docs.title: CLI Usage
docs.text: Rivet is currently used through the rivet command-line compiler.

docs.title: Installer Script
docs.text:
Rivet provides install.sh for release-based installation:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/diveshkshirsagar/RIVET/main/install.sh | bash

Supported installer environment variables:

  • RIVET_VERSION (default: latest, example: v0.0.1)
  • RIVET_INSTALL_DIR (default: /usr/local/bin)
  • RIVET_REPO (default: diveshkshirsagar/RIVET)
  • RIVET_DRY_RUN (set to 1 to preview install path without changing files)

docs.title: Command Shape
docs.text: ./build/rivet <source_file.rvt> [options]

docs.title: Core Options
docs.text:
• --dump-ast
  • Prints parsed AST for debugging.
  • --target=<triple>
  • Overrides LLVM target triple.
  • --mcpu=<cpu>
  • Sets CPU model for backend code generation.
  • --flash-origin=<addr>
  • --flash-size=<size>
  • --ram-origin=<addr>
  • --ram-size=<size>
  • Memory-layout parameters for embedded-oriented builds.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Basic compile:

./build/rivet tests/validation.rvt

Compile and print AST:

./build/rivet tests/validation.rvt --dump-ast

Cross-target compile options:

./build/rivet tests/validation.rvt \
  --target=arm-none-eabi \
  --mcpu=cortex-m4

docs.title: Practical Notes
docs.text:
• The compiler prints LLVM IR to stdout as part of normal execution.
  • If main() exists in your source, Rivet wires it into __rivet_entry.
  • If no input file is provided, Rivet exits with usage guidance.

docs.title: Low-level Features
docs.text: Rivet exposes a few low-level constructs so you can experiment with memory and bitwise behavior while keeping syntax readable.

docs.title: Bitwise and Logical Operators
docs.text:
Rivet uses keyword operators for bitwise and logical actions:

  • and
  • or
  • lsft
  • rsft

Example:

int flags = 1;
flags = flags lsft 2;
flags = flags or 3;

docs.title: References and Explicit Addressing
docs.text:
int base = 10;
int ref ptr = address_of base;
int value = deref ptr;

These are useful for modeling pointer-like operations and testing dereference semantics.

docs.title: Array Indexing
docs.text:
Array indexing compiles into offset calculations over a contiguous integer block:

int[3] nums;
nums[0] = 7;
nums[1] = nums[0] + 1;

docs.title: Current Caveats
docs.text:
• There is no raw pointer type beyond ref constructs.
  • No heap allocation or manual memory release is available yet.
  • Some semantic checks are still strict or incomplete.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Rivet is an early-stage compiler, but it already emits direct LLVM IR for core operations. This page explains how to think about performance today.

docs.title: What Is Fast Today
docs.text:
• Integer arithmetic and comparisons map directly to LLVM instructions.
  • Local variables are stack-allocated and accessed with load/store.
  • Loops compile to simple control-flow blocks.

docs.title: Where Overhead Can Appear
docs.text:
• Imports inline all parsed nodes, which can increase compile time for large trees.
  • Some semantic checks are conservative and may reject edge cases.
  • String handling is still evolving and may change structure in future revisions.

docs.title: Practical Tips
docs.text:
• Keep loops simple when testing performance paths.
  • Prefer integer math in hot paths.
  • Use --dump-ast only when debugging; it adds runtime overhead during compilation.

docs.title: Roadmap Ideas
docs.text: Future improvements may include richer optimizations, more aggressive constant folding, and expanded IR analysis. For now, the primary focus is correctness and clarity.

docs.title: Control Flow
docs.text: Rivet supports block-based if/else, while, and for loops. All control-flow bodies are parsed as blocks ({ ... }).

docs.title: if / else
docs.text:
if (condition) {
  // statements
} else {
  // statements
}

Notes:

  • Conditions must be wrapped in parentheses.
  • else is optional.
  • In codegen, conditions are treated as integers: zero is false, non-zero is true.

docs.title: while
docs.text:
while (condition) {
  // statements
}

The loop re-evaluates the condition before each iteration.

docs.title: for
docs.text:
Rivet supports two for loop forms.

Range-style loop:

for (i in 0 to 10 step 1) {
  // statements
}

Array-iteration loop:

for (pin in pins) {
  // statements
}

Notes:

  • step is optional; if omitted, a step of 1 is assumed.
  • The identifier before in is always the loop iterator name.
  • to is inclusive of the upper bound in current tests.
  • In array iteration, the iterator receives each element value in order.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
int i = 0;
int sum = 0;

while (i < 5) {
  if (i == 2) {
    sum = sum + 10;
  } else {
    sum = sum + i;
  }
  i = i + 1;
}

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text:
• break and continue are not implemented yet.
  • Single-line bodies without {} are not supported in the parser.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text: Rivet supports user-defined functions using fun and return.

docs.title: Declaration Form
docs.text:
fun int add(int a, int b) {
  return a + b;
}

Return type can be int, str, or void.

docs.title: Calling Functions
docs.text:
fun int add(int a, int b) {
  return a + b;
}

fun int main() {
  int result = add(2, 3);
  return result;
}

Arguments are comma-separated expressions.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Supported parameter forms include:

  • Plain values: int x, str name
  • References: int ref p
  • Optional references: int optref maybe

docs.title: Return Statements
docs.text:
fun int identity(int x) {
  return x;
}

fun void log_value(int x) {
  return;
}

docs.title: Current Limits
docs.text:
• Function overloading is not supported.
  • Type conversions are not implicit; argument and return types must match expected forms.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text: This page introduces variables as implemented in Rivet today. You will see how to declare values, assign them, and work with arrays and references.

docs.title: Integer Variables
docs.text:
int x;
int y = 42;
  • int x; is valid and defaults to 0 in codegen.
  • int y = <expression>; evaluates the expression and stores the result.
  • Declarations end with ;.

docs.title: String Variables
docs.text:
str message = "Hello Bare Metal";
str label;

label = "RIVET";
message = label;

Strings are first-class values in the current prototype. Assignments between str values are allowed.

docs.title: Fixed-Size Arrays
docs.text:
Rivet supports fixed-size arrays of integers using bracket syntax:

int[5] nums;
nums[0] = 10;
nums[1] = nums[0] + 5;

Array indexing works in expressions and assignments. Index expressions must resolve to integers.

docs.title: References (Address and Dereference)
docs.text:
Rivet models references using address_of and deref:

int base = 42;
int ref ptr = address_of base;

int roundtrip = deref ptr;

Use int ref to declare a reference. The deref operator reads the value at the referenced location.

docs.title: Assignment Rules
docs.text:
Assignments are binary expressions with =:

int i = 0;
i = i + 1;

Current rule: the left-hand side must be a declared variable or an array element.

docs.title: Scope Notes (Current Implementation)
docs.text: Variables are tracked in a shared name map for codegen and semantic checks. For now, keep names unique within the same block to avoid accidental shadowing.

docs.title: Memory Model
docs.text: Rivet models memory explicitly so newcomers can understand how values are stored and accessed. The current implementation focuses on stack allocation and simple references.

docs.title: Stack Allocation
docs.text:
When you declare a variable, Rivet allocates a stack slot in LLVM IR:

int x = 7;

This becomes an alloca and a store in LLVM, and reads become load instructions.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
References are created with address_of and read with deref:

int base = 42;
int ref ptr = address_of base;
int value = deref ptr;

Use references when you want explicit address manipulation in your program logic.

docs.title: Arrays in Memory
docs.text:
Fixed-size arrays are allocated as a block of contiguous integers. Indexing compiles into pointer arithmetic on that block.

int[3] flags;
flags[0] = 1;
flags[1] = 0;

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text:
• Only stack allocation is modeled for now.
  • There is no heap allocation or dynamic array support yet.
  • Null reference handling is still being refined.

docs.title: Modules and Imports
docs.text: Rivet uses a simple import system that loads other .rvt files and injects their AST nodes into the current module.

docs.title: Import Syntax
docs.text:
import dummy;

The parser reads the target module, parses its contents, and places them into an ImportAST node. During codegen, imported nodes are emitted before the current file continues.

docs.title: Import Resolution Paths
docs.text:
The current implementation searches for module files in:

  1. lib/<module>.rvt
  2. ../lib/<module>.rvt (fallback when running from build directories)

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Imports are cached to avoid duplicate loads.
  • Cyclic imports are prevented by tracking module names.

docs.title: Types
docs.text: Rivet is a small language prototype, but it already includes a few core types that appear throughout the compiler and tests.

docs.title: int
docs.text:
The primary numeric type is int:

int count = 10;
int total = count + 5;

int values are currently represented as 32-bit integers in LLVM IR.

docs.title: str
docs.text:
Strings are supported through the str keyword:

str message = "Hello Bare Metal";
str label;

label = "RIVET";
message = label;

The backend lowers strings to a small struct containing a pointer and length.

docs.title: References (ref)
docs.text:
References use the ref keyword combined with address_of and deref:

int base = 42;
int ref ptr = address_of base;

int roundtrip = deref ptr;

References are useful for modeling memory access and pointer-like behavior in tests.

docs.title: Arrays
docs.text:
Rivet supports fixed-size arrays of integers:

int[4] nums;
nums[0] = 1;
nums[1] = 2;

Array indexing works on both the left and right side of assignments.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• void exists as a token, but full function signatures are still under construction.
  • The type checker continues to expand; some edge cases are still being refined.

docs.title: LLVM Backend Details
docs.text: This page explains how Rivet lowers language constructs into LLVM IR in the current implementation.

docs.title: Module and Entry Function
docs.text:
Codegen initializes:

  • LLVMContext
  • IRBuilder<>
  • Module named Rivet Bare Metal Module

Top-level code is emitted into:

define i32 @__rivet_entry() {
entry:
  ...
}

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
int x = 7;

Becomes roughly:

%x = alloca i32
store i32 7, ptr %x

Variable reads use load.

docs.title: Binary Operators
docs.text:
Current mapping:

  • + -> CreateAdd
  • - -> CreateSub
  • * -> CreateMul
  • / -> CreateSDiv
  • and -> CreateAnd
  • or -> CreateOr
  • lsft -> CreateShl
  • rsft -> CreateAShr
  • == -> icmp eq then zero-extend to i32
  • != -> icmp ne then zero-extend to i32
  • < -> icmp slt then zero-extend to i32
  • > -> icmp sgt then zero-extend to i32
  • = -> store into variable slot and return RHS value

docs.title: If / Else
docs.text:
If creates blocks:

  • then
  • else
  • ifcont

The condition is tested against zero for branch selection.

docs.title: While
docs.text:
While creates blocks:

  • cond
  • loop
  • afterloop

Flow:

  1. branch to cond
  2. evaluate condition
  3. branch to loop or afterloop
  4. loop body branches back to cond

docs.title: For
docs.text: for lowers to a loop with a dedicated induction variable and a step value. It uses the same structure as while, but emits initialization and increment logic around the loop body.

docs.title: Strings
docs.text: Strings are represented as a simple struct containing a pointer and length. The backend builds a String struct type in the LLVM context and reuses it for string values.

docs.title: Imports and IR
docs.text: ImportAST::codegen() emits all imported nodes before continuing with the importing file. This effectively injects imported declarations and statements into the same module.

docs.title: Current Backend Limitations
docs.text:
• Unary lowering is not fully implemented yet.
  • Function declarations are not yet integrated into parser and codegen.
  • Some edge cases in array and reference semantics are still being refined.

docs.title: Internals Overview
docs.text: This page describes the current compiler pipeline as implemented in this repository. It is intended for readers who want to connect the language features to the codebase.

docs.title: High-Level Architecture
docs.text:
Rivet uses a classic frontend + LLVM backend structure:

  1. Lexer (src/Lexer.cpp)
  2. Parser (src/Parser.cpp)
  3. AST (include/Rivet/AST.h, src/AST.cpp)
  4. Codegen Context (include/Rivet/CodeGen.h, src/CodeGen.cpp)
  5. Driver (src/main.cpp)

docs.title: Lexer
docs.text:
The lexer reads a file stream and emits integer tokens:

  • Keywords are negative enum values (for example tok_if, tok_import).
  • Single-character operators and punctuation are returned as ASCII values.
  • Line and column are tracked for diagnostics.
  • Line comments (//) are supported.

docs.title: Parser
docs.text: The parser is recursive descent with a precedence-aware binary expression parser.

docs.title: Statement entry points
docs.text:
Current statements include:

  • import <id>;
  • variable declarations (int, str, int ref, arrays)
  • if (...) { ... } [else { ... }]
  • while (...) { ... }
  • for (i in start to end [step step])
  • for (item in arrayName)
  • blocks { ... }
  • expression statements
  • empty statement ;

docs.title: Expression parsing
docs.text:
Primary expressions include:

  • number literals
  • string literals
  • identifiers and calls
  • parenthesized expressions

The ParseBinOpRHS function applies operator precedence for binary expressions.

docs.title: Import flow
docs.text: ParseImport resolves the module name, avoids duplicate imports, and parses the imported file into an ImportAST node. Import search paths currently include lib/<module>.rvt and ../lib/<module>.rvt.

docs.title: AST Layer
docs.text:
Key AST nodes include:

  • literals and variables (NumberAST, StringLiteralAST, VariableAST)
  • declarations (VariableDeclAST)
  • operators (BinaryOpAST, UnaryOpAST)
  • control flow (IfAST, WhileAST, ForAST, BlockAST)
  • calls and imports (CallAST, ImportAST)
  • memory nodes (AddressOfAST, DerefAST, IndexAST)

Each node provides dump() for debug output and codegen() for LLVM emission.

docs.title: Driver (main)
docs.text:
The driver:

  1. Loads the source file.
  2. Parses to a top-level AST node list.
  3. Optionally dumps the AST.
  4. Initializes the LLVM module context.
  5. Builds a synthetic entry function __rivet_entry.
  6. Codegens each top-level node.
  7. Emits a return if the block lacks a terminator.
  8. Prints the full LLVM IR.

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text: This page explains how the Rivet repository is organized and where to find the core compiler components.

docs.title: Key Directories
docs.text:
• include/Rivet/ - Public headers for the compiler (AST, Lexer, Parser, SymbolTable, Type, CodeGen).
  • src/ - Implementations of the core compiler modules.
  • tests/ - Sample .rvt files used for parser and semantic coverage.
  • docs/ - MkDocs site sources and Doxygen configuration.
  • lib/ - Importable Rivet modules (used by import).
  • examples/ - Example programs or experiments.

docs.title: Core Files
docs.text:
• include/Rivet/AST.h / src/AST.cpp - AST node definitions and codegen.
  • include/Rivet/Lexer.h / src/Lexer.cpp - Tokenization and lexing logic.
  • include/Rivet/Parser.h / src/Parser.cpp - Recursive descent parsing logic.
  • include/Rivet/CodeGen.h / src/CodeGen.cpp - LLVM context setup.
  • include/Rivet/SymbolTable.h - Scope and symbol tracking.
  • include/Rivet/Type.h - Type system definitions.
  • src/main.cpp - Compiler driver and entry point.

docs.text: For a complete class breakdown and dependency graphs, see the C++ API Reference. It is generated with Doxygen and includes class hierarchies, include graphs, and symbol indexes.

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text: This page lists Rivet language keywords you can use in source files in v0.0.1.

docs.text:
• int
  • str
  • void
  • ref
  • optref
  • null

docs.text:
• fun
  • return
  • import

docs.title: Control Flow
docs.text:
• if
  • else
  • while
  • for
  • in
  • to

docs.title: Operators (Keyword Form)
docs.text:
• and
  • or

docs.title: Memory Helpers
docs.text:

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• and, or, lsft, and rsft are binary operators.
  • not and - are unary operators.
  • __volatile_store(address, value) is available as a compiler intrinsic call form.

docs.title: Syntax Reference
docs.text: This is a compact syntax guide for writing Rivet programs in v0.0.1.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
A file may contain:

  • import statements
  • variable declarations
  • function declarations
  • control-flow and expression statements

docs.title: Imports
docs.text: import dummy;

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
int x;
int y = 10;
str message = "Hello";
int ref p = address_of y;
int optref maybe = null;
int[4] nums;

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
fun int add(int a, int b) {
  return a + b;
}

fun void nop() {
  return;
}

docs.title: Control Flow
docs.text:
if (x == 0) {
  x = x + 1;
} else {
  x = x + 2;
}

while (x < 10) {
  x = x + 1;
}

for (i in 0 to 10 step 1) {
  x = x + i;
}

for (item in nums) {
  x = x + item;
}

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text:
Primary forms:

  • integer literal
  • string literal
  • identifier
  • function call
  • parenthesized expression
  • address_of <identifier>
  • deref <expression>
  • array index arr[i]
  • null

Operators:

  • assignment: =
  • arithmetic: +, -, *, /
  • comparison: <, >, ==, !=
  • keyword operators: and, or, lsft, rsft
  • unary: -, not

docs.title: Statement Endings
docs.text:
• Declarations and expression statements end with ;
  • Block/control structures use { ... }
